title: IdentityProviderCatalog
description: Vendor knowledge `zitadel setup` scaffolds connection files from, keyed by the entry's default slug. Bundled so scaffolding works offline; the table ages with the installed CLI, and the written connection file stays tenant-editable. Adding a provider is a data change to this table.

propertyNames.$comment: Every key but the editor pointer is a provider, and doubles as the default connection slug, so it obeys the slug grammar `idp-connection.json` enforces.

display_name.description: Written to the connection as `display_name` and shown on the sign-in button.

template.description: Written to the connection as `template`. Keys vendor knowledge only (glyphs, the setup scan/match, claim tables); it carries no protocol behaviour.

console_url.description: The vendor console where the developer registers the OAuth application. Surfaced during the announce step and in error envelopes.

docs_url.description: The vendor's own integration documentation, surfaced alongside `console_url`.

callback_guidance.description: Whether the vendor accepts many redirect URIs on one client, or needs an application per environment. Surfaced during the announce step to guide app registration.

protocol_block.description: Merged into the scaffolded connection file verbatim. Holds vendor conduct only: the prompted `client_id`, the derived `client_secret` reference, `slug`, `display_name`, `template`, `claim_mapping` and `provisioning` are composed at scaffold time, never stored here.

claim_table.description: Maps a user-schema property name to the provider's documented claim name. Authored per provider, not derived. At scaffold the rows whose key the active schema defines become the connection's `claim_mapping`; the rest stay unmapped.

additionalProperties.description: An exact top-level claim key: no path syntax, and `$`-prefixed values are reserved.
